The "one world at a time" behavior is "typical" only because the outgoing WID for transactions is "typically" determined by a register. At least that's how it seems to me after thinking about it. I could have tried to do it by negation, by suggesting that the one-world-at-a-time behavior occurs when the outgoing WID is "_not_ determined by the properties of the transaction itself".
